assessmentSettings.gradingCalibration: Grade the understanding shown. Accept equivalent wording, reasonable rounding and simulation precision; do not demand repeated units already supplied by a blank or an explanation that the blank did not request. For written responses, credit correct concepts, methods and consistent follow-through. Deduct for the original error without repeatedly penalizing its correctly carried-forward consequences. Preserve deductions for materially wrong values, misconceptions and missing required work. Binary completion items remain binary. Check the published assignment version and its actual question numbers before grading.

questions.prompt: Identify one change between Dive, Neutral, and Spread in your formation dive. Describe the motion or graph before and after it, then explain how your speed or altitude gap changed relative to your partner. You may use approximate readouts OR a specific qualitative graph change, such as a line rising, flattening, or falling; exact numbers are not required.

questions.prompt: Explain your formation strategy in four short parts: (1) how body position changed drag and your steady falling speed; (2) when you opened the parachute relative to your partner and why; (3) a feature from the velocity-time graph and a feature from the acceleration-time graph, including the deployment change; and (4) why your partner can appear to move upward while still falling. Use your run as evidence. Qualitative graph descriptions or approximate readings are both acceptable.
